python_dash_c_ephemeral.message:
NO EPHEMERAL python -c EXECUTION ALLOWED!
Write a real script file in the project directory and run it.
WHY: python -c invocations are non-persistent, hide logic, cannot be reviewed, debugged, or re-run, and routinely deadlock claude when they fail silently.
DO THIS INSTEAD:
  1. Write the code to ./scripts/<task>.py (or ./tmp/<task>.py inside the project)
  2. Run: .venv/bin/python ./scripts/<task>.py

node_dash_e_ephemeral.message:

dev_null_suppression.description: Block any redirection to /dev/null - it always hides valuable output
dev_null_suppression.message:
NO REDIRECTING TO /dev/null ALLOWED!
This ALWAYS hides valuable output, errors, and warnings.
WHY: When a command fails, the error message is the most important thing to see. Suppressing it routinely deadlocks claude because the failure mode becomes invisible.
DO THIS INSTEAD:
  - Run the command and let it write to stdout/stderr
  - If you must check for command existence, use: command -v <name> ; echo "$?" (no /dev/null)
  - If the output is truly noisy, write it to a project-local log file: ./tmp/cmd.log

Use a project-local ./tmp/ directory instead.

background_amp_run.message:
NO BACKGROUNDING COMMANDS WITH TRAILING & ALLOWED!
WHY: backgrounded shells orphan their output and routinely cause claude to wait forever for a result that never returns.
DO THIS INSTEAD: use the Bash tool's run_in_background parameter — it captures output the harness can read.

az_discrete_all.description: Block ALL discrete az commands - must use turnkey scripts in .utilities/.azure/
az_discrete_all.message:
ABSOLUTELY NO DISCRETE 'az' COMMANDS ALLOWED — EVER, NO EXCEPTIONS!
This covers show/list/get/login/logout AND every mutation verb.
WHY: discrete az invocations are non-persistent, leave no audit trail, hide failures, and cannot be re-run by the user. They routinely deadlock claude when they hang on auth, prompt for input, or fail silently.
DO THIS INSTEAD:
  1. Write a turnkey bash script in `.utilities/.azure/`
  2. The script must read credentials from the pack-root `.env`, log every action, and be re-runnable
  3. Refer to: `.utilities/.azure/AZURE_GUIDELINES.xml`

junk_directories.description: Block reading/searching/editing files inside generated, cached, or vendored junk directories
junk_directories.message:
what the fuck are you doing looking here?
These aren't the droids you're looking for.....

You tried to read, search, or edit a generated/cached/vendored junk directory:
  __pycache__/  node_modules/  dist/  build/  target/debug/  target/release/
  .pytest_cache/  .mypy_cache/  .ruff_cache/  .tox/  .next/  .nuxt/  .turbo/
  .gradle/  .terraform/  .cache/  .parcel-cache/  bower_components/
  *.egg-info/  .DS_Store  .git/objects/  .git/logs/  *.pyc  *.lock  *.min.js  etc.

These files are auto-generated, vendored, compiled, or cached. They tell you NOTHING about the user's actual code. Reading them just burns context window and surfaces noise.

DO THIS INSTEAD:
  - Read the SOURCE files (src/, lib/, app/, the actual hand-written code)
  - Run the build/tooling that produces the artifact instead of inspecting the artifact
  - If you genuinely need a third-party library's source, install it as a dep and read from the package's published source — not from node_modules or .venv/lib

rust_build_rs_creation.description: Block creating new build.rs files without explicit user authorization
rust_build_rs_creation.message:
BLOCKED: Creating build.rs is FORBIDDEN without explicit user authorization!

build.rs has significant build-system, security, and reproducibility implications:
  - Every println!("cargo::rustc-...") alters compilation globally
  - RUSTFLAGS injection via build.rs affects all downstream crates
  - Build scripts execute arbitrary code at compile time

If build.rs is genuinely required, STOP and ask the user first.
Document every cargo directive with an inline comment explaining WHY it is needed.
Refer to: ~/.codex/enforcement/guidelines/guideline_documents/xml/rust_guidelines.xml

no_truncation_or_inline_tee.description: Block 2>&1, | tee, head, and tail in Bash commands. These indicate non-persistent logging and output truncation.
no_truncation_or_inline_tee.message:
BLOCKED: 2>&1, | tee, head, and tail are UNACCEPTABLE.
  - 2>&1 + tee: indicates the script is NOT properly persistently logging.
    Fix: write to a real log file from inside the script (>> /path/to/script.log).
  - head/tail: indicates output is being truncated for readability.
    Fix: write the full output to a file, then grep/awk what you need.
